result.title: An Interpretable Fuzzy Tree for Turbofan Remaining Useful Life with an Auditable Per-Component Diagnostic Layer
result.summary: Data-driven remaining useful life (RUL) estimators for turbofan engines are accurate but opaque, and their internal features typically encode remaining life rather than any specific component's state. This paper presents an interpretable genetic fuzzy tree that predicts RUL from cruise-condition sensor means on N-CMAPSS while exposing a per-component diagnostic layer inspectable rule by rule. The tree follows the engine hierarchy: sensors to component health, then to bounded component damage, spool damage, and RUL, so each level answers a different maintenance question. Training is staged so the prognostic objective cannot reshape the diagnostic layers: health leaves are fitted to physical targets and frozen, a deterministic fuzzy damage map with fleet-referenced thresholds is imposed on each component, and only the aggregation is optimized for RUL. It consumes 13 cruise-mean scalars per cycle rather than a trajectory, which removes any sequence model. On the native split it reaches 8.44 cycles RMSE on the multi-fault subset and 11.51 across all modes with 333 free parameters, 411 total rules, 32 to 12,000 times fewer than compiled baselines. An exhaustive sensor search bounds which components are diagnosable under the tested cruise-mean design, and the rule base is structured to admit formal verification, which this study does not discharge.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 N-CMAPSS 上用可解释遗传模糊树从巡航均值传感器预测涡扇发动机剩余寿命，按「传感器→部件健康→部件损伤→RUL」分层，采取分阶段训练：先以物理目标拟合并冻结健康层，再加确定性命中模糊损伤映射，仅优化上层聚合，以约 333 个自由参数取得竞争性 RMSE。
AI.relevance_reason: 其分层健康/损伤状态抽象，以及「冻结证据层、只训练聚合层」的分离监督，可能为 LVR 中潜状态是否被下游目标侵蚀、证据层与回答层贡献分配提供类比线索，但领域与视觉推理相距较远，具体可迁移性需人工核查。
